# Explicit column breaks

These six original controls are generated by `tools/column_break_fixture.py`
using the repository's original `exhausted-cell-indents.docx` package scaffold.
They contain only authored text and formatting, with no corpus content or
embedded fonts. Regeneration changes ZIP timestamps; the committed packages
are the exact bytes opened for the retained native reference PDF references.

The reference application exported the PDFs without saving changes to the source DOCX.
Each JSON records the source and PDF SHA-256 hashes. The controls use Arial
10 pt, exact 12 pt lines, half-letter pages, half-inch margins, and either one
column or two equal columns with a quarter-inch gap.

The cases exercise an inline break, a terminal break before another paragraph,
a leading break, repeated breaks crossing a page, and inline/terminal breaks in
a single-column section. A terminal column break moves the paragraph mark into
the next column, consuming a line before the following paragraph. This differs
from the default terminal page-break compatibility behavior.

Most text positions were extracted from the native PDFs using pypdf. In the
inline PDF, the `After` ActualText record has dummy coordinates. Its reference
position (162.07 pt, baseline 45.62 pt) was supplied after inspecting the native reference
render and checking the second-column origin and first-line baseline. It is a
geometry expectation corroborated visually, not a precise extracted measurement.
The browser checks use a 0.15 pt tolerance and check baselines only when Arial
is available. They do not establish pixel-identical glyph rasterization.

Unit and browser tests cover layout, caret hit testing, selection, editing,
undo, package-part preservation, export/reopen, Ctrl+Shift+Enter, and plain-text
copying. Six sources plus 19 browser exports passed 50 XML schema checks.

Relevant clauses: ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.3.1 and 17.18.4. The latter explicitly
requires advancing to the next page when no further column is available.
Continuous section transitions and breaks inside table cells or shape text are
outside this implementation's supported subset.
